newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T sets up project-specific firms.
newsitem.headline: India L&T sets up project-specific firms.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) said on Friday it had set up two companies to execute specific projects taken up on the build-own-operate-transfer (BOOT) basis.
Several more similar projects were in the pipeline, the firm said in a statement released at its annual general meeting.
"The company is bidding for several projects on a BOOT basis and the company may have to make investments in special purpose vehicle companies to be formed for taking up such projects," L&T said.
Analysts say that BOO and BOOT techniques have proved the most efficient way of financing the long-term projects required to shore up India's crumbling infrastructure sector.
L&T has geared up to execute them with a will.

L&T set up a separate company called the Haldia Cogeneration Ltd. after it won a contract to construct and operate a combined cycle cogeneration power plant with Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd. on a build-own-operate (BOO) basis, the statement said.
L&T took a 74 percent equity stake in the 4.7-billion-rupee project, amounting to 866 million rupees, it added.

L&T also set up the Narmada Infrastructure Construction Enterprise Ltd., to convert a two-lane bridge into a four-lane bridge across the Narmada river in the western state of Gujarat, the statement said.
"L&T will invest 300 million rupees by way of equity in this company for a 60 percent stake," the firm said. "The estimated cost of the project is 1.3 billion rupees."
